newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: MOTOR RACING-BERGER UNSURE ABOUT FUTURE IN FORMULA ONE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BERGER UNSURE ABOUT FUTURE IN FORMULA ONE.

text.p: Formula One driver Gerhard Berger said on Saturday he would probably quit the Benetton team and might give up Grand Prix racing altogether.

In an interview with Austrian radio ORF, Berger, who has missed the last two races because of a sinus infection, said: "Today I am not able to say if I will compete in Formula One next year. I will make a decision about my future in August."
The Austrian driver also said he did not know if he would be physically fit to take part in the British Grand Prix next weekend.
Berger said he doubted if Benetton would be the right team for him should he continue in Formula One next season. His contract with the Italian team expires at the end of the year.
He said he was in contact with the Williams team.
Berger last seriously considered retirement after the deaths of compatriot Roland Ratzenberger and Brazilian three-time world champion Ayrton Senna at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix.
